rationale: Real bug from eval/realbug-queue/apistar-staticfiles-resource-leak.json (encode/apistar, BSD-3-Clause, bugfix_confidence 0.70, archived repository). resource-leak is thinly represented in v2 (2 cases); this adds a real async-specific instance of the pattern.

provenance.provenance_notes: Reconstructed from a real apistar bug fix: an async static-file handler opened a file handle without guaranteeing it was closed on every code path. No apistar static-file serving code is reproduced -- function name, file path, and surrounding code are invented. The diff below is the reverse of the historical fix: it replaces the context-manager-guarded open with a manual open/close pair that has an await in between, reintroducing the leak.

ground_truth.explanation: The file handle is now opened and closed manually instead of via a context manager, with an await between open and close. If run_in_threadpool(handle.read) raises or the coroutine is cancelled while awaiting, handle.close() on the next line never executes, leaking the file descriptor. Under sustained traffic to a static-file endpoint this accumulates open file descriptors until the process hits its limit.
